title: Implement soft-cancel and progress resilience for compact action surfaces
creator: Priya Kapoor
description: Users and engineers are seeing inconsistent behavior between 'loading' and 'disabled' states across compact and icon-only button variants. This causes layout shifts when spinners appear, confusing affordances for cancelable actions, and theme mismatches (spinner color or contrast inconsistent in dark modes). This ticket designs and specifies a 'soft-cancel' UX pattern and a resilient progress affordance that reduces layout shift and clarifies action state across variants and themes.
background: Recently multiple regression issues were reported from SDK integrations and a mobile POC where icon-only actions would jump when a spinner replaced an icon. Design QA flagged color contrast failures for white-on-light spinner in elevated surfaces. PM flagged a customer incident where a long-running request left the button permanently disabled with no clear cancel path. Engineering proposed a 'soft-cancel' API but needs a complete spec for visuals, motion, and a11y behavior.
acceptance_criteria: Spinner placement does not introduce horizontal or vertical layout shift for compact and icon-only variants
All variants (primary, secondary, ghost, icon-only, compact) have a documented loading token set that defines spinner color, size, and offset for light/dark/contrast themes
Implement 'soft-cancel' pattern: during long-running ops the action surface shows cancel affordance without fully disabling other interactive surfaces (spec + microcopy)
ARIA and screen reader flow: loading state announced via polite live region and cancel control is keyboard accessible with clear label
Design tokens and migration notes provided for engineering: token names, fallback rules, and example theme overrides
Design review approval from Product and Engineering and a verified visual QA checklist completed against latest console theme snapshot
decisions: Adopt 'soft-cancel' where the primary action transitions to a secondary cancel affordance after 900ms for long ops (instead of full disable)
Prefer inline micro-spinner (16px) that sits within the existing icon bounds with token-driven negative margin to avoid relayout
For icon-only buttons use a fixed-size invisible placeholder to reserve layout and avoid width changes
Spinner color will be derived from a new token --button-loading-foreground which maps per theme and contrast, falling back to token --button-foreground
tradeoffs: Soft-cancel improves recoverability but adds interaction complexity (additional keyboard target and state transitions to test)
Reserving layout with placeholders slightly increases DOM weight for icon-only buttons, but eliminates visual jitter which was higher priority
Using token-driven negative margin requires careful cross-platform token translation for mobile SDKs; engineering asked for explicit migration notes

Verify no width/height layout shift occurs when loading starts (compare snapshots)

Confirm telemetry events for cancel interactions are emitted and documented
